issue_context.title: systemd-networkd assertion failed and lost internet connection after resume from suspend
issue_context.body:
At first I thought this issue was related to #17803, but even after Arch maintainer [backported](https://github.com/archlinux/svntogit-packages/commit/bb0ca6bd29043205c5bdfbe7b449be04d608e373#diff-3e341d2d9c67be01819b25b25d5e53ea3cdf3a38d28846cda85a195eb9b7203a) the patches to the systemd package, the issue still remains. So I guess this is another issue.

**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > 247.1-3 Arch Linux build

**Used distribution**
 > Arch Linux

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
 > 5.9.13-arch1-1
 
**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > x86_64

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > Reconnect to my acccess point after resume from suspend.

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > systemd-networkd doesn't reconnect to my AP automatically after resume from suspend.

**Steps to reproduce the problem**

I'm using systemd-networkd and iwd for wireless settings.

1. At first boot, internet connection works fine.

2. Execute `$ systemctl suspend`, and open the laptop lid to resume from suspend.

3. After repeating resume from suspend two or three times (mostly two times in my case), systemd-networkd raises assertion error, but still reconnects to the network correctly at this point.

```
Assertion 'IN_SET(link->state, LINK_STATE_CONFIGURING, LINK_STATE_FAILED, LINK_STATE_LINGER)' failed at src/network/networkd-address.c:934, function address_handler(). Aborting.
```

4. After another repeating resume from suspend two or three times (mostly one or two times in my case), systemd-networkd doesn't establish the connection.

- Manually restarting `systemd-networkd.servise` or `iwd.service` makes internet connection work again.

- systemd-networkd works properly by downgrading systemd to the previous version.

```
$ sudo pacman -U /var/cache/pacman/pkg/systemd-246.6-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
```

`$ journalctl -u systemd-networkd`

review_comments: Shouldn't the condition below be inverted? I.e. only do further processing only when `link->state` is `LINK_STATE_CONFIGURING`? Right now potentially we'd do that also on `LINK_STATE_UNMANAGED` and others.
Yeah. But, I'd like to leave that to another PR. Currently, `link->state` conditions are borked in many places. I'd like to rewrite related code comprehensively later.
